newsitem.title: CHINA: PEAC WEIGHS MANILA-MACAU BAE 146 FREIGHTER SERVICE.
newsitem.headline: PEAC WEIGHS MANILA-MACAU BAE 146 FREIGHTER SERVICE.

text.p: Pacific East Asia Cargo Airlines Inc (PEAC) is considering a three times a week freighter service between Manila and Macau, the airline's managing director,Benjamin Solis, told Reuters.

The head of the Filipino regional express cargo airline, also the Philippines cargo flag carrier, visited Macau airport this week to finalise plans for the service using a British Aerospace Plc 146 freighter.
"A lot of groundwork has already been done but it would be an experiment for us as the Macau market is completely unknown," Solis said.

If the go-ahead is given, the first all-cargo airlink is expected to begin within 90 days. The proposed service follows the recent signing of an air services agreement between the Philippines and Macau which saw the green light for an Air Macau passenger service.
PEAC's new day time service will provide greater aircraft utilisation for the carrier's two BAe 146 jet freighters which are mainly used at night, industry sources added.

The airline now flies to Hong Kong, Jakarta, Seoul, Taipei and Singapore but by summer 1998 would like to add two or three Asian cities to its overnight network. PEAC already has traffic rights for Kuala Lumpur, Penang and Bangkok.
Solis said he hopes to add three Boeing 727 freighters to its fleet of one Boeing 727 with 25 tonnes capacity and two 10 tonne capacity BAe 146s.
And despite the current weight restriction controversy facing B727 converted freighters, Solis said it is the right aircraft for PEAC.

PEAC has long standing plans to begin a freighter link between Manila and China but Solis said the company has been frustrated by China and the Philippenes being unable to negotiate their first cargo aviation services agreement despite five years of talks.

PEAC would like cargo services to Shanghai, Xiamen and Guangzhou. Negotiations have taken place with China Southern Airlines under which PEAC would provide a freighter in exchange for a code-share agreement between Guangzhou and Manila but an agreement there has also proved elusive, Solis said.
Industry sources that the carrier's rival, Philippine Airlines is expected to start a passenger service to Shanghai in October.
